body.statement: As an immediate corollary of the simultaneous-event theorem, \(\widehat{\mathrm{CI}}_n=[\widehat L_n,\widehat U_n]\) satisfies \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}:\,\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing}P\{\Theta(P)\subseteq\widehat{\mathrm{CI}}_n\}\ge1-\alpha\). The interval is intersected with \([-K,K]\), and coverage allows \(R(P)=0\), nonunique optimizers, and binding obstacle constraints.
body.justification: Uniform coverage is the direct reportable consequence of the root inclusion-event and endpoint theorem.
body.gap: Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) treat finite moment systems, whereas this corollary inherits a primitive uniform boundary-regression and signed-measure inclusion theorem for a continuum completion class. It does not characterize the source paper's separate parametric estimator.
body.consumer: County-level temperature and other continuously changing policy panels can report one confidence interval covering every full-law-compatible WAOSS value.
